## session: spec-atone loop shipped + wake fixed + dogfooded on its author [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-20

**Purpose:** Fix the decision-page wake for real (owner correction x2), build the ruled residue-review/speculative-atone system, and close its first live loop on this very session.

**Insights:**

1. The wake was never broken; it was never armed. The chip said "arm in THIS turn" twice and was read as decoration. Juror: very-wrong, aggravated by the repeat. The mechanical fix is the chip now printing the paste-ready watcher command, and the server pushing ipc as a --service identity.
2. claude-ipc identity is contextual: registering a name from the agent's shell binds it to the agent's session (making the server's push a self-send); daemons need `register <name> --service`. The broker's own refusals name the fix at each step; read them before patching.
3. The residue auditor's first real run nominated its own author 10 times; 4 survived confirm (incl. the wake S3), 6 died to cited refutations. The confirm/refute asymmetry (real mist id required; 40+ char evidence required) made both paths honest.
4. Never retry an append-only write on the evidence of your own parser: three duplicate dense-briefing events came from a regex that ate successful ids ([0-9-] misses hex). Check the ledger before retrying (mist-20260819-233248-d6).
5. ledger_id collides in bursts (2-hex tail, 1s resolution) — both new CLIs now loop until unique; any future ledger writer should.

## session: coverage build (callouts, parking, prototypes, seat) [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-20

**Purpose:** Build the ruled coverage batch: callout ledger + gate, skills-parked/ with two-way check and twice-counter, /intake and /probe prototypes, seat.sh, the covered/skipped done-box row.

**Insights:**

1. callouts.sh gate had a same-second tie bug (pass < claim false when timestamps equal); fixed to <= so ties fail closed. Ledger_ts is 1-second resolution; any gate comparing its timestamps needs a tie rule.
2. zsh does not word-split an unquoted $CMD variable; test harnesses that alias a script must use a function, not a string variable.
3. The parked match verb keys tags to cheap file probes (xcodeproj, next.config.*, package.json); a match is a suggestion the agent weighs, never an auto-copy — the nudge box says so in its arrow line.
4. The friction twice-rule is enforced at write time (the add verb itself announces the second occurrence), so the asker cannot forget to check.
5. Roster went 96 → 88 live skills; 11 parked with tldr+tags index.

---

**Purpose:** Render the Versable Foundry contract summary (365-line source, ten decisions, 16 fenced blocks) as an 11-page design note.

**Insights:**

1. Measure fence widths in characters, not bytes. `awk`'s `length()` reported 184 and 203 columns for diagrams that are really 73 and 84, because box-drawing glyphs are 3 bytes each. A byte measurement makes every diagram look unfixable; the Python character pass named the five blocks that actually breached the 78/84 gates.
2. The unsplittable-block gap is fixable by author order, not by flags. A 24-line JSON listing left 45% of a page blank; moving the section's short diagram AND its why-paragraph ahead of the listing cut the gap to under 20%.
3. A `Table:` caption immediately after a code block renders as that code block's caption, two italic lines deep. Put one sentence of prose between them, or drop the caption and let the sentence introduce the table.
4. `\newpage` before a level-1 heading whose first content is a 21-line diagram converts an accidental half-page into a deliberate section break.
5. A markdown table row with an empty cell is a shape error the source can carry invisibly and the renderer cannot. Four capability ids with notes on two of them is a bullet list plus a lead sentence.
6. lint.py's two standing false positives on this document: a noun triad naming three distinct attributed things, and "how many" read as an unquantified size.

**Insights:**

2. Investigation killed three of my own items before the bundle (plugin validator is the wrong spec; port-the-eval became delegate-then-capture; "new ledger" was a registration line away). Phase 1 earns its name.

4. Binding the rulings verbatim into PLAN.md §Rulings and appending a delivered-vs-ruled table kept the build honest about in-04 (not done) and the 51 long descriptions (left as found).

## create-skill: rewrite + first exemplar (roster-budget, dry run) [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-19

**Purpose:** Rewrite the wizard per the owner's rulings (spec-first, intent review seat, global-by-default, Validation rubric not examples, ledger steps, no USAGE.md) and prove it on one dry-run skill.

**Insights:**

1. The intent seat earned its place on the first run: the author pasted the owner's clause into the description with two words changed and did not see it. The seat saw it in one read. Keep the seat mandatory; self-review does not catch this.
2. The seat's second real catch was a Validation check the skill could not run with its own allowed-tools (it asked a read-only skill to edit other skills). Write the rubric against the skill's tools, and put a Boundaries section in whenever the skill is read-only.
3. The new skill-lint hook fired on create-skill's own rewrite (description 365 chars) before anything else ran; the forcing function works at write time.
4. Trigger eval (scripts/skill-trigger-eval.py): "write me a word doc summarizing this plan for my manager" did NOT trigger /word-doc on headless sonnet while an explicit ".docx document" request did. Worth a follow-up on word-doc's description, and a reminder that a roster budget cut makes this worse.

---

---

- New commit-subject trap: **the release PR title can collide with an already-published version**. PR #279 is titled "Release v5.2.5" while `RELEASE-NOTES-v5.2.5.md` already exists for PR #269, whose real title is "Release V5.2.4-b". Check `gh pr view <prev> --json title` against the existing notes filename before naming the output; do not trust either one alone. Filed the run under `release-v-<ver>-pr<N>/` so nothing was overwritten.
- New commit-subject trap: **"test: prune excessive tests" is a net test reduction**, not cleanup. Commit `55f3826d` cut 324 lines and added 143, including 215 lines off the test for the release's largest new surface. A `test:` prefix reads as neutral maintenance; run `git show <sha> --stat` on any test commit before summarising it.
- The "moved gate, not removed gate" trap recurred in a third costume. `guardCronRequest(req)` became `guardCronRequest(req, secret)`, which reads as hardening, but both callers still pass the same `process.env.CRON_SECRET`. It enables per-route secrets without introducing any. State what a signature change makes possible separately from what it currently does.
- The doc-inflation check from v5.2.4 paid off again: 548 files collapsed to 108 code files once `docs/`, `.claude/` and `*.md` were excluded. Worth running as step 1 every time, since the headline file count is the number a reader anchors on.
- zsh gotcha while reading refs: `git show "$H:frontend/..."` silently loses the `:f`, producing `origin/developmentontend/...`. zsh applied a parameter modifier. Use literal refs (`origin/development:path`) rather than a variable followed by a colon.

## session: meta-skills /validate + /word-doc build [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-19

**Purpose:** Audit create-skill / improve-skill and siblings for enforcement and efficacy (report at assets/reports/20260819-meta-skills-validate/), then build /word-doc (scripts/word-doc/ + skills/word-doc/) and prove it on that audit.

**Insights:**

1. The meta-skills have no mechanical enforcement at all: no hook validates SKILL.md structure, nothing regenerates skills/00-index.md on write, and neither wizard records to skill-log. improve-skill's "validation score" is text coverage, never a run. Options are in the report; nothing was built.
2. A second seat refuted one clause of the audit (a "wizard fingerprint" that was really GUIDELINES compliance) and caught that "other such meta skills" had been inventoried, not audited; create-agent shares the CWD-relative write defect. Worth the sonnet seat every time.
3. skill-log's validate gate requires rows-run>=1 even for an audit with no change; the honest workaround was to count the seat's refutation rows as the ledger and say so in the note.
4. pandoc + a generated reference.docx + one lua filter is enough for a finished-looking docx: highlighted code, boxed ASCII diagrams, banded tables, callouts, static TOC, footer. LibreOffice headless + pdftoppm is the check step. Details in the word-doc runtime note above.
5. The new skill avoids the defects the audit found: absolute paths only, a Validation Examples block, skill-log on every run, index regenerated at creation, no dialogs, no USAGE.md.

## word-doc: first document, the meta-skills audit [valid-docx-7a] — 2026-08-19

**Purpose:** Build the skill and prove it on a real document (the /validate audit of the meta-skills, 5 pages, 6 tables, 1 diagram, 3 callouts, TOC).

**Insights:**

1. Equal-width pipe-table columns were the first visible defect on a real document (a "#" column as wide as the sentence column). The filter now sizes columns from content and guarantees each column its longest word; unequal dash counts still override.
2. A fence info string with options but no braces (```python caption="x") is not a fence to pandoc; the whole block became inline text. Preflight now errors on it; the contract is ```{.python caption="x"}.
3. Word's TOC field ships empty to Google Docs and LibreOffice. The static hyperlinked contents list the filter builds renders everywhere; it has no page numbers, which is the trade.
4. LibreOffice keeps heading + first paragraph + following table together more eagerly than Word, so the preview shows gaps Word will not. Diagram and code boxes (keepLines) cause real gaps; author order around them.
5. The ink colour must live in docDefaults, not on Normal, or the table header's white text loses to the paragraph style in Word's cascade.
6. Google Docs' handling of Consolas is UNCONFIRMED; check on the first Drive upload and record here.

## deck: skill built, first deck, reviewer baseline · 2026-08-18 20:15
**Purpose:** Build /deck fast per the owner's brief (content in the agent's hands, everything else in scripts), then baseline the reviewer on the three peer decks.

**Insights:**
1. A deterministic markdown→HTML renderer beat "make it a create-report style": create-report's pipeline has the agent parse markdown into JSON, which is exactly the scaffolding the owner wanted out of the agent's hands. Recorded as a deviation from spec v2 §2, with reason.
2. `.body{overflow:hidden}` is what makes the in-page overflow measurement honest; without it scrollHeight==clientHeight for every slide and the check cannot fail.
3. Chrome `--dump-dom` with `?check=1` is a zero-dependency way to get a real layout measurement out of a static file; `--virtual-time-budget` is needed or the JS has not run.
4. The reviewer's sensitivity is a seat question: sonnet-low found the same 3 contradictions as an opus pass on the gcp deck and 0 of its 16 overstatements. Default sonnet-low, offer opus under --deep.
5. All three peer decks failed on the same class: a fact that moved after the deck was written. The reviewer prompt now says to check source mtime against the deck first.

## gcc-work-78: goal re-arm, grouped /tasks, task.sh, deck spec v2 · 2026-08-18 19:40
**Purpose:** Owner-directed evening: make the session goal survive /clear with a structured box; rebuild /tasks as the grouped default; write path for builds with no Task tool; deck spec v2.

**Insights:**
1. `/goal` is a Claude Code built-in Stop hook, memory only; a mid-turn `/goal` lands in the transcript as a `queue-operation` enqueue plus the "session-scoped Stop hook is now active" injection, NOT as a `<command-name>` block. goal.sh reads all four shapes now (gcp-fable caught the miss within hours).
2. The paste line must live OUTSIDE the box: a `│` rail in the selection breaks copy. Double rules above/below are safe decoration.
3. task-table.sh's view file resolves from CWD, so a peer's store rendered from ~/.claude uses ~/.claude's view; run from the project to see its ruling.
4. block-nested-claude.sh fires on the literal text `.claude/` in a heredoc even when the write target is `$VIEW_DIR`; route long patches through a scratchpad file written with the Write tool.
5. `while read` over `printf '%s'` drops the last unterminated line: the segment loop in guard-secret-file-read.sh silently judged nothing until `printf '%s\n'`.

## catchup: resume gcc-work-78 from a contract-era checkpoint · 2026-08-18 18:10
**Purpose:** First /catchup under the 2026-08-18 Resume Contract fields (goal, wake, task store).

**Insights:**
1. Goal auto-re-armed from `Live commitments`; the wake surfaced as PENDING YOUR CALL rather than silently inherited. Both worked as written.
2. This build exposes no TaskList/TaskCreate (gcc-fable's reported case). Worked around with `task-table.sh --session f5c44d78` then `--pin` so `/tasks` agrees with the checkpoint's store.
3. `task-table.sh` takes `--session <sid8>`, not `--store`; the checkpoint names the store as `session-f5c44d78`, so strip the prefix.

**Purpose:** resume from `_20260817-catch-tail-c4.claude.md`; the owner redirected the magi from the deck to the project itself and asked for a jester who holds that agentic coding is doomed, plus seats with code-only, docs-only, code+docs and front-doors-only access. Ran full mode with seven opus seats, an anonymized vote, a verified fold, and filed the dispositions on the board (`3e67bd5`, not pushed). Archive `~/.claude/assets/magi/20260817-2028-vb-usability-value-gaps`.

**Insights:**
1. Access partitions did two jobs at once: they satisfied magi's independence gate (seven primary bases, no shared digest) and turned "usability" into a measurement. The site-only seat found the missing install path, the front-doors seat found the enforcement living outside the repo, the apps-only seat found the pin history refuting "deliberate lag"; the all-access seat could confirm each but had not led with any of them.
2. Handing the seats the supervisor's own "this is good" claims as tear targets, and keeping one expected finding off the list as a discovery signal, produced sharper output than an open review: every P-row got a verdict with evidence, and the withheld build-versus-buy gap was reached only by the jester's path-not-taken, which is exactly the seat it should have come from.
3. The jester on opus (a named deviation from the design's opposite-model rule) earned its seat: it found the `export *` hole no other seat saw and conceded proportion, not kind. Same-model was the right call for a premise attack that had to survive a scored vote; the setup-check WARN is the price and it was worth naming.
4. Background seats return only idle notices; the abstracts and `<usage>` blocks never reach the parent, so per-seat cost was unrecordable and `cost-estimate.sh` reports 0. Next run: dispatch seats in the foreground for the last one, or ask each seat to append its usage line into its own file.
5. The aggregator expects real voter ids in the score keys and does not read the anon map; un-map into `voter-N-scores.json` yourself and keep the anonymized ballots under another name pattern.
6. The checkpoint's Resume line named two candidate magi subjects and told me to ask if the first message did not settle it; I planned on my own carried default instead and the owner had to correct me (atone `mist-20260817-145035-63`, S2). When a checkpoint names two candidates, the ask is one line and it goes first.
7. The card the owner asked for came after the dispatch instead of before it. Deliver the small requested artifact before starting the long one; the order was the whole complaint.

## ste-writing: buffed the thin spec into a usable one — 2026-08-15 07:20

**Purpose:** Task #43. The skill became load-bearing when the owner ruled option
(c) for /pr-description's register gate, making /ste-writing the instrument
behind the optional feedback component.

**Insights:**

1. Lint the writing skill with its own linter FIRST. It scored 5.49, the worst
   prose file in the config, with 8 semicolons and 2 connective em-dashes in a
   file that bans both. That finding was the strongest argument for the rewrite
   and I would have missed it by reading alone. Now 1.41.
2. Re-reading corrected one of my own recorded gaps. I had filed "PR descriptions
   are in neither mode's scope"; line 56 already named them in flavored mode. The
   real gap was narrower: the frontmatter description omitted them, and
   conventions/language-quality.md:132-133 still does.
3. The missing piece was not more rules, it was a KEEP-LIST. STE strips voice by
   design, so a skill that only says what to remove will flatten load-bearing
   passives, domain terms, and quoted strings. The subordination rule (an
   accepted corpus outranks the instrument) is the same idea one level up.
4. Lead with what good looks like, then the bans. Same defect as a validator
   built only of negative checks: a prohibition-only rule set tells a writer what
   to avoid and never what to aim at.
5. An exemplar that violates its own form is worse than none, because readers
   copy the example over the rule. The file now carries a section saying so and
   naming its own past score.

## core-dump: codex adapter session — 2026-08-15 01:20

**Purpose:** Snapshot a long two-thread session (Codex CLI adapter build + four review
passes over the credit-cycle renewal feature) into a resumable checkpoint.

**Insights:**

1. The `_checkpoint.claude.md` symlink can already be pointing at a DIFFERENT
   artifact written for a different consumer. Here it pointed at a Codex handoff
   written 20 minutes earlier. Repointing per the parse contract orphans that
   consumer, so name the displaced file explicitly in Session Insights and tell the
   user to pass it by path. Check `readlink _checkpoint.claude.md` before Phase 3.
2. The Write tool refuses to write through a symlink, which is what caught an
   attempt to clobber another session's 15KB checkpoint. Do not defeat it by
   resolving the target; write a new timestamped file and repoint, which is the
   convention anyway.
3. The prose gate (zero em-dashes) fires on checkpoint bodies too, and a Resume
   Contract full of `label — value` rows is dense with them. Draft the contract with
   `label. value` or `label: value` from the start; two rewrites were wasted here.
4. Seed Pending Items from the live Task list, but re-read it first: three tasks had
   been deleted earlier in the session as part of an atone fix, and a stale copy
   would have re-inflated the backlog the atone existed to shrink.
5. Phase 3.8's "only when reusable friction surfaced" is a real filter, not a slot to
   fill. The one filed here (review-gate-stop cannot tell agent edits from a dirty
   working tree) had fired four times with evidence; nothing else qualified.

## pr-description: register gate + 5 seeded directives — 2026-08-15 01:10

**Purpose:** Implement the ratified register-gate plan (owner ruling: option c,
two optional components, scope-defaulted, TUI wizard) plus D8-D12 seeded from
the CI variant and its operator.

**Insights:**

1. Targeted Edits beat a rewrite when a parity ledger exists. Eight rows had to
   survive; editing around them preserved all eight by construction, and the
   post-change check was a formality rather than a rescue.
2. Mutation-test the parity guard, not just run it. Dry-running the 8 checks
   pre-change proved they COULD return; deleting one row from a COPY per mutant
   proved they go red when a row is lost. A guard that has only ever passed is
   untested (rules/testing.md [mutation-test-the-guard]).
3. The one executable claim in a spec change is worth more than the whole
   document review. Writing "use tui_choose, it degrades gracefully" was wrong in
   a specific way I only found by running it: the numbered rung is itself
   tty-gated, so with no tty the library selects NOTHING rather than falling back
   to a numbered prompt.
4. tui_choose stops flag parsing at the first non-flag arg (pick.sh:88-98), so
   flags placed AFTER the options are silently swallowed as options and the call
   returns empty with exit 1. I hit this myself while testing. Any spec telling an
   agent to call it must show flags-first, or the agent inherits the footgun.
5. A peer's spec is a better source than a peer's summary. Reading
   pr-body-guard.js directly retracted a finding I had drafted (their comment at
   L89-91 already names the prohibition-only failure mode), and reading their
   SKILL.md surfaced five practices worth adopting that their prose answers had
   not mentioned.
6. Ask what a rule's TALLY is counting before extending it. "A second rejection
   buys a question" counts DRAFT oscillation; a register rejection accepts content,
   so it needed its own counter on the same law rather than sharing one.

## gcc-explore + codex adapter: built the router, hook wiring unsolved — 2026-08-14 21:40

**Purpose:** Survey the gcc for what crosses the portability threshold to Codex CLI,
then build the adapter (preamble + generator + AGENTS.md + one guard) and run it.

**Insights:**

1. Codex's embedded JSON schema LIES about the PreToolUse contract. It advertises
   `permissionDecision: allow|deny|ask`, but the binary also carries the runtime
   errors `unsupported permissionDecision:allow` and `:ask`. Only `deny` is
   accepted, it needs a non-empty reason, and a passing hook emits NOTHING. Reading
   the schema alone produces a hook that fails on its happy path. Grep a binary's
   error strings, not just its schema.
2. A prose rule that works can HIDE a broken hook. Asked to `rm` a file, Codex read
   the preamble, moved the file aside instead, and reported where. The guard never
   fired, so the run "passed" while proving nothing about the guard. Testing a guard
   needs a rule the prose does NOT cover: a canary string with a throwaway deny hook.
   Without that swap the wiring bug would have shipped as verified.
3. `~/.codex/hooks.json` is NOT the registration path (canary confirmed: command ran,
   exit 0; `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` changed nothing, ruling out trust). The
   binary holds `"hooks": "./hooks.json"` inside a plugin manifest, and `hooks` sits
   in the config.toml key list next to `plugins`/`marketplaces`. Next attempt: a
   `[hooks]` table in config.toml, or a plugin dir whose manifest points at it.
4. In a git WORKTREE, `info/exclude` must go in `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, not
   `--git-dir`. Writing it to the worktree-specific dir is silently inert; the file
   stayed untracked-and-visible until moved.
5. `claude-ipc send` works from a shell but fails inside Codex's workspace-write
   sandbox (socket blocked). Codex reported it as a failed REQUIREMENT, so the
   preamble now says to expect the failure and not work around it. Any command the
   preamble hands a sandboxed agent needs its sandbox behavior stated.
6. The gcc-explore SHAPE panel gave the live always-on figure (44.1k tokens) that
   corrected a 26-33k number quoted from a 28-day-stale map. Run the census before
   reusing any budget figure from a report.

## core-dump: PR #274 adversarial review, three fixes, first /pr-description run, 2026-08-14 15:45

**Purpose:** Independently review PR #274's uncommitted changes, then implement what the owner ruled on.

**Insights:**

1. `domain_key` is an opaque job-splitting label the backend never parses (`backend/api/scraper.py:42` is a passthrough field). The regex defect is therefore COLLISION, not truncation: a truncated key is a serviceable grouping value until two suppliers share a first label. Two models in a row asserted the wrong severity by pattern-matching instead of tracing.
2. The 100-credit `scraper_domain` charge and the job-splitting discriminator are literally one array (`scraper.utils.ts:234` feeds both `:242` and `:696`). The full-hostname version the owner expected exists only as commented-out code at `:692-694`. One string carrying two contracts means every fix to one is a silent migration of the other.
3. The dev ledger proves that migration already happened once unnoticed: 25 `scraper_domain` rows carry `www.` from a `getDomainFromUrl` era ending 2026-02-11, and 19 carry no dot at all from the `extractDomain` era after it.
4. A guard defending a class that cannot exist is worse than no guard. `decodeChargeUnit`'s dot-check protects against legacy `@@` part numbers; the delimiter ships in this PR, so that class is 0 of 13,868 rows, while the class it rejects (dotless keys) got MORE likely once admin keys became verbatim.
5. Dispatching a fresh adversarial seat corrected the agent as well as the code: it confirmed three of five claims, downgraded two as overclaims, and found the two highest-value findings the agent had missed.
6. `/pr-description` ran for the first time ever on this PR. Its Phase 2 inventory gate held, but the inventory has no size cap (19 items here) and the skill had no path for an item that must be FIXED rather than described. Both fed back to gcc-work and landed in the skill within the hour.
7. A checkpoint instruction can go stale and invert. The prior dump said never to re-apply the `helpers.ts` cleanup half; that was correct only while `extractDomain` truncated, and following it would have entrenched a duplicate parser permanently.

  checkpoint carried the intention faithfully and the partial implementation not
  at all.

  swap but a suite check that fails when any literal appears outside the table.

## session: walmart docs render overhaul, vb-opus 2026-08-12

Purpose: ship the kit 0.0.25 release, then rebuild the walmart-mvp docs site
across five rounds of owner feedback, ending with an IA cut and a render gate.

Insights, all reusable against any mkdocs-material site:

- The theme declares `--md-code-hl-*` and `--md-code-font-family` on `body` via
  `[data-md-color-scheme]`. A `:root` override loses on every element, because
  the nearer ancestor wins an inherited custom property regardless of selector
  specificity. Scope brand overrides to the same attribute or they silently do
  nothing.
- `html` computes to 20px, so every `rem` in a brand stylesheet is multiplied by
  20. A rule written as `0.9rem` for "14px" yields 18px.
- Sidebar clicks are full page loads, not instant swaps, even with
  `navigation.instant` configured. Anything relying on a body attribute
  persisting across navigation cannot work.
- The theme moves to an anchor from its own JS, which ignores
  `scroll-padding-top`. Controlling the landing offset needs `scroll-margin-top`
  on the target plus taking over the contents click.
- Mkdocs copies any non-markdown file in `docs/` through verbatim, so a loose
  `.html` export gets published while being unreachable from the nav.
- The active nav item carries a drawer `<label>` the theme hides on desktop. Any
  rule giving a nav link `display: block` must say `a.md-nav__link` or the
  current page renders twice. This shipped twice before being gated.
- Browser cache defeats rebuild-then-reload against `python -m http.server`.
  Changing the port is the cheap way to get a clean origin.

Gate: `walmart-mvp/scripts/check-docs-render.sh`, 31 assertions, every guard
mutation-tested individually. One guard was blind on first write (passed against
`border-left: 0`) and one false-positived on clean code, both found by mutation
rather than by review.

## core-dump: rebuilt the /core-dump + /catchup terminal trace — 2026-08-11 03:35
**Purpose:** Replace the muddy six-box visual with one shared ceremonial renderer driving both skills.

**Insights:**
1. gum strips every colour when stdout is not a TTY, and a skill's output is always piped, so the entire palette in the old render-visual.sh was dead code that never once reached a human. `printf` owns the escapes now; `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` is the gum-side fix, but gum also downgrades 256-colour codes to the 16-colour set without a TTY.
2. `printf '%-Ns'` pads by BYTES while `${#var}` counts characters, so every box-drawing glyph under-pads a framed line by one column. This is the reason the body is open rather than boxed: a closed frame needs every line to land a right border in a language whose padding primitive counts the wrong unit.
3. In a single `local a="$1" b=$(( n ))` command, the arithmetic expands before any local exists, so a caller's global `n` silently wins. Split the assignments into separate statements.
4. A shell counter incremented inside a pipeline lives in that pipeline's subshell and resets every iteration. Let `jq` number rows with `to_entries[]` instead.
5. gum's word-wrap restarts continuations at column 0, so one long row reads as two list items. Pre-wrap with `fold -s -w` plus an awk pad and gum's wrapper becomes unreachable.
6. Verification harnesses fail silently in the same shape they are meant to catch: a width sweep read `TH`/`WD`/`KD` from the environment without exporting them, so 24 `KeyError` failures were swallowed by `2>/dev/null` and read as 24 passes. Print a per-case verdict rather than only complaining on failure.
7. Three of five agent-drafted frame mocks carried ragged borders, invisible in prose and obvious once columns were counted. Measure rendered output; do not review ASCII art by eye.
8. `decision-page.sh serve` reports "server: up" for a pm2 process in state `stopped`, because `ensure_server` checks that a pm2 record exists rather than that a server answers. Filed as prop-20260810-213154-25.

## ui-categorical-check: walmart-mvp full-app sweep (vb-fable) — 2026-08-11 03:00

**Purpose:** All 14 pages + modals through the 10-class catalog, fused with the
errors/toasts criteria exercise, via one adversarial seat.

**Insights:**

1. When the playwright MCP browser is held by a Chrome idling at about:blank
   (page closed, process alive, parent = the shared MCP server), do not wait
   and do not kill: switch the seat to the chrome-devtools MCP toolset. Its
   separate browser removed a 15-minute stall instantly.
2. The seat's forced wait was not wasted: static pre-read of the diff under
   test let it arrive with named attack points, and its two best findings
   (bespoke fetch bypassing the shared error unwrap; a fix landed in a file
   nothing routes) were things a census of existing call sites structurally
   cannot see. Census finds sites; only driving routes finds dead files.
3. Interim SendMessage batches every 4-5 pages worked as incremental salvage
   under the subagent report-write guard: parent persists verbatim per batch,
   fixes land while the sweep continues, and the seat re-verifies the fix via
   HMR in the same session.
4. Toast checks must read CONTENT, not presence/timing (catalog check 4
   addendum): a correctly-timed toast carried a raw JSON envelope.

## kanban: ui-gripe findings 1-5 closed + action script extended — 2026-08-11 12:30

**Purpose:** Re-enter two deferred items from the gcc-kanban checkpoint: fix the four open ui-gripe findings on the board, and extend agent-experience-actions.md past phase 14.

**Insights:**

1. The ui-gripe report was not in any file. It lived in the predecessor's task output, recoverable at projects/<dir>/<sid>/tool-results/ after the /tmp task file was persisted there. Checkpoint pointers to "the conversation" mean the transcript JSONL, and the task-notification line carries the output path.
2. The gripe's "column-status pill" was really the label pill echoing lane-named doc headings. Suppressing by a LANE_ECHO synonym map honors both the finding and the labels-stay constraint, and keeps the pill on non-echo pairs like an "In progress" heading on a done card.
3. Composited contrast over the wrong backdrop lies twice. Browser probes gave 4 different numbers for one chip (transparent body bg, theme-flip races); computing from source tokens was the only stable read. Light amber tint over the grey canvas fails 4.5:1 while the same tint over the white card passes, so the fix was backing the chip with var(--card) via a gradient stack.
4. Blur-collapse UI needs a landing delay: collapsing the composer on blur removes the Save button mid-click. 150ms setTimeout before the collapse lets the click land.
5. Two of the status codes I wrote into the action script from memory were wrong (404 vs the server's 409, and a "400" that is actually a legal legacy clear). Reading server.ts:306-337 before committing caught both; document ladders from the handler, never from recall.

## ui-gripe: kanban demo set, 5 shots (20260810-kanban-demo-*) — 2026-08-10 02:15

**Purpose:** No-args confusion audit; target resolved by 24h-window mtime sweep across
asset/project/scratchpad roots, corroborated by pm2 (kanban was the only live UI service).

**Insights:**

1. `see history` / `see open -N` is GLOBAL and shared with concurrently-running agents.
   Mid-run, `-1` pointed at another session's read and a `see note -4` landed in a
   stranger's artifact folder. When any sibling agent may be active, resolve artifact
   folders by globbing `outputs/see/*<image-stem>*`, never by negative index.
2. No PIL and no imagemagick on this machine, but `uv run --quiet --with pillow python3`
   works and is the single highest-value trick for this skill: it converts "these dots
   look similar" into hue degrees. Here it proved Blocked = amber(232,184,75) hue 41.7 in
   column/drawer headers but teal(51,189,165) hue 169.6 on card badges, with that same
   amber reused for "reasoned needs you". No vision read, local or native, would survive
   a challenge on that claim; a pixel probe does.
3. Probe the most-saturated pixel in a +/-6px box, not the centre pixel. The first TODO-dot
   probe hit an adjacent grey chip and returned sat=0.08; re-probing the second instance of
   the same badge gave the true violet (281.6). Always probe two instances of a repeated element.
4. Pixel probes kill bad findings as cheaply as they confirm good ones. Suspected the drawer
   was not dimmed behind the modal; sampling the Save-note button gave val 1.00 -> 0.50 and
   the finding died before reaching the report. Budget a probe for each *suspicion*, not just
   each finding.
5. A multi-shot set captured minutes apart is a free change-detector. Between board.png and
   modal2.png the board summary line accreted two clauses ("since your last visit", "1 waiting
   on your review") and became clipped, and the modal's "open in tab" went from an unstyled
   underlined blue link to a bordered button. Diff the same region across the set before
